caption.v0: Move the sliders like warming the sensor in your hand or breathing on it: the AHT20 follows within a second.
caption.v1: Climb the slider: pressure falls about 12 hPa for every 100 m, so the BMP280 can tell which floor you are on.
caption.v2: Tilt the board: the MPU6050 feels gravity on three axes and the bubble level shows the angle the firmware works out.
caption.v3: All three sensors share the same two wires. The station reads them in turn and sums the room up in one word.

bus.diagram: I2C bus: the ESP32-S3 and three sensors sharing 3V3, SDA, SCL and GND, each sensor with its own address
bus.pullups: SDA and SCL need pull-up resistors (most sensor boards have them built in)
bus.fact1: Two signal wires for every sensor: SDA carries the data, SCL the clock the ESP32-S3 sets.
bus.fact2: Each sensor answers only to its own address, so many can share the bus.
bus.fact3: An I2C scan at start-up lists who is there: the quickest way to find a loose wire.
